title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap & Pricing (Q4 2026)
author: Ayesha Kapoor
body:
Summary:
This document consolidates the product overview, PRD-level requirements, high-level design specs, roadmap themes for the next two quarters, pricing and packaging guidance, and release notes for the Unified Inference initiative (hosted API + Dedicated + Private parity). It is intended for PMs, Eng, SRE, Sales, and Solutions Engineering.

Objectives:
- Deliver a single developer experience across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments with consistent API semantics and predictable economics.
- Reduce per-token unit cost by 20% through runtime and routing improvements while maintaining baseline quality.
- Enable enterprise adoption through Private deployment hardening (KMS, audit logging, VPC templates).

Scope:
- API: text generation, chat, embeddings, streaming, function-calls (no model training).
- Runtime: kernel selection, quantization profiles, KV/prefix caching, batching.
- Operations: Rollouts (canary/A-B), tracing, per-route SLOs, fallback policies.
- Billing: unify usage metrics (tokens & embeddings) across deployment modes.

1) Product Overview
Introduction:
Unified Inference consolidates Redwood's serving capabilities into a single product narrative: same API surface and SDKs, consistent SLAs, and cost-aware routing. The product targets engineering teams who need predictable latency and cost without sacrificing model quality.

Core capabilities:
- Unified API: identical REST/SDK interfaces across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Support for streaming, structured outputs, and tool/function calling.
- Model Catalog: curated open models, Redwood-verified performance profiles, and compatible quantized variants.
- Smart Routing & Fallbacks: policy-driven routing by latency, cost, region, and tier with automated fallback to compatible model variants.
- Optimize Module: automated batching, cache hints, and quantization recommendations per workload.
- Observability & Control Plane: per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and rollout primitives (canary, A/B, traffic shaping).

User personas and success metrics:
- Developer (PLG): time-to-prototype < 1 hour, first successful call within quickstart.
- Platform Engineer: predictable p99 latency within 1.5x of SLA in production; 99.9% availability for Dedicated pools.
- Product Lead: unit cost reduction target of 20%+ YOY.

2) PRD: Requirements (MUST / SHOULD / MAY)
Overview: The PRD defines functionality required for GA of Unified Inference core feature set.
Must-have requirements:
1. API compatibility: Existing Redwood API endpoints (v2) must return identical response schemas across deployment modes for the same model variant.
2. Model pinning & rollout controls: per-route model version pinning, canary percent traffic, automatic rollback on error rate > 1%.
3. Observability: per-request tracing IDs, token-level cost breakdown, p50/p95/p99 latency metrics, throughput (rps) charts.
4. Security & Compliance: KMS integration for customer keys (Private), TLS mutual auth for Dedicated, audit-log export to S3/GCS.
5. Routing policies: configurable by latency, cost, region, and custom tags.
6. Billing: accurate token/embedding metering within 0.5% error for invoicing.

Should-have requirements:
- Quantization profiles: presets (int8, int4) validated for top-5 supported models with guidance on expected quality delta.
- Auto-batching suggestions: Analyze request shape and recommend batching window (ms) and max batch size.
- SDK convenience functions: streaming helpers, response validation utilities, and retry strategies.

May-have requirements:
- Per-tenant on-disk KV cache for low-latency prefix-serving (beta).
- On-prem operator for air-gapped deployments (installable package for advanced customers).

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end smoke tests passing for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private with a canonical prompt set (see section "Quality Benchmarks").
- Performance targets: p95 token latency within 1.8x of baseline for single-shard models; throughput scaling linear within 10% for dedicated pools up to target capacity.
- Billing reconciled in sandbox account within 0.5% versus ground truth.

3) Design Specs (High level)
3.1 Architecture diagram (textual):
- Control Plane: API gateway, routing service, model catalog service, rollout manager, billing/usage service.
- Data Plane: serving runtime (GPU/CPU workers), cache layer (Redis for ephemeral KV), batch scheduler, telemetry exporter.
- Integrations: KMS, SSO/SCIM, telemetry sinks (Datadog, Honeycomb), object stores for audit logs.

3.2 Runtime considerations:
- Kernel selection: runtime queries kernel catalog using model arch + seq_len histogram -> choose kernels optimized for attention type (flash attention, tiled matmul).
- KV/prefix caching: store hot KV caches in GPU memory where possible, fallback to host memory with async prefetch.
- Batching strategy: continuous batching with max latency budget (configurable per-route). Default latency budget: 40ms for interactive routes, 200ms for high-throughput batch routes.

3.3 Model variants and compat matrix:
- Provide compatibility table for model families (Llama2-13B, Mistral-7B, Redwood-6B) and recommended quantization profile.
- Each variant entry: model_name | architecture | recommended_quant | expected_tokens_per_sec | quality_delta_AB (vs fp16).
Example table (text):
| model_name | arch | quant | tps | q_delta |
| Llama2-13B | transformer | int8 | 120 | -0.8% |
| Mistral-7B | transformer | int4 | 210 | -1.5% |

3.4 Operational controls:
- Rollout manager supports rules: canary(percent), time-window, automatic rollback threshold (5xx rate > 0.5% for 5m) and manual override.
- Circuit breaker: per-route failure budget; on exceeding error budget, traffic is routed to fallback model variant and an alert is created.

4) Roadmap & Themes (Next 6 months)
Theme A: Performance & Cost (Q4 2026 – Q1 2027)
- Milestones:
  - Oct 2026: Kernel selection v1 (production rollout) — fallback kernel path & metrics.
  - Nov 2026: Continuous batching defaults + per-route latency budgets.
  - Dec 2026: Quantization-presets v1 and validator + documentation.
  - Jan 2027: Optimize module V2 (auto-batching suggestions + cache hints).
Expected impact: 15–25% cost reduction for typical RLHF chat workloads.

Theme B: Enterprise Readiness (Q4 2026)
- Milestones:
  - Nov 2026: KMS/HSM integration test plan complete; Private deployment audit logging GA.
  - Dec 2026: VPC templates + deploy validation for on-prem packages.
  - Feb 2027: Advanced RBAC + SCIM provisioning for Private control plane.
Expected impact: Unlock Dedicated/Private contracts worth $X–$YM ARR (sales estimate).

Theme C: Developer Experience & PLG (Q4 2026 – Q1 2027)
- Milestones:
  - Oct 2026: Quickstarts + SDK streaming helpers.
  - Nov 2026: Console per-route SLO views + rollout UI.
  - Jan 2027: Guided Optimize recommendations in Console.
Expected impact: Faster onboarding and higher self-serve conversion.

Roadmap Gantt (text):
- Oct–Nov 2026: Kernel selection + Quickstarts + Console SLO views.
- Nov–Dec 2026: KMS tests + Quantization presets + Rollout manager improvements.
- Dec 2026–Feb 2027: Optimize v2 + RBAC + Packaging improvements for Private.

5) Pricing & Packaging Notes
Goals:
- Keep PLG-friendly entry point while enabling committed pricing for Dedicated.
- Price signals should encourage use of cost-saving features (quantized variants, caching, batching).

Pricing tiers (proposal):
- Developer (Hosted, self-serve): pay-as-you-go tokens/embeddings; free tier 1M tokens/month; standard latency SLO best-effort.
- Team (Hosted + Dedicated trial): monthly commit discount (10% off list) with soft limits; console SLOs and basic telemetry.
- Enterprise (Dedicated & Private): annual reserved capacity pricing, premium SLAs (99.9% uptime), advanced security add-ons (KMS/HSM, audit retention).

Credits & Discounts:
- Quantized model variant discount: 15% lower token rate for int8/int4 variants flagged in catalog.
- Caching credit: effective billing discount applied when per-route cache hit rate > 50% (measured monthly). Implementation note: cache credit applies as billing rebate, not real-time discount.

Metering details (billing accuracy requirements):
- Tokens counted by normalized_token_units (NTU) using tokenizer mapping (consistent with open-source tokenizer library).
- Embedding units measured per 1536-dim vector or fraction thereof.
- Reconciliation window: 48 hours for usage reporting; invoices generated monthly.

6) Release Notes (v1.0 GA — 2026-11-15)
Key highlights:
- Unified API parity across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (same v2 endpoints and schemas).
- Kernel selection v1 deployed to production for Llama2-13B and Mistral-7B families.
- Quantization-presets (int8) available in catalog for top-3 models with validation reports.
- Console: per-route SLO dashboard and rollout manager UI (canary + manual rollbacks).
- Billing: unified token metering with 0.3% variance validated in sandbox.

Known issues & workarounds:
1. Private on-prem installer: large clusters (>16 GPUs) may require manual host-level kernel tuning. Workaround: follow onprem-packaging/runbook tuning steps (link to runbook).
2. Streaming SDK edge-case: stray EOF errors on long-lived connections under heavy load; workaround: client retry policy with exponential backoff (sample code in SDK docs).

Operational runbook (summary):
- Pre-deploy checklist:
  1. Run end-to-end smoke tests against canary (use canonical prompt set).
  2. Confirm model catalog hashes and quantization validator checksums.
  3. Ensure telemetry endpoints are healthy (Datadog/Honeycomb).
- Rollout steps:
  1. Deploy model variant to 1% canary for 15 minutes.
  2. Monitor p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, and cache hit rate.
  3. Increase to 10% for 30 minutes if metrics stable.
  4. Full rollout with gradual traffic increase over 2 hours.
- Rollback criteria:
  - 5xx rate > 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes.
  - p99 increase > 2x baseline for 10 minutes.

Quality benchmarks (test harness):
- Canonical prompt set: 250 prompts across instruction, chat, summarization, and retrieval-augmented use cases.
- Regression threshold: mean ROUGE-2 drop <= 1.2% and model toxicity failure <= 0.1%.
